hero.eyebrow: Freelance developer · React & Next.js · Brasília, BR
hero.lead: Nine years building web and mobile products — from first commit to recurring revenue. Interfaces that hold up under real users, plus the part nobody wants: performance, billing and deploys.
hero.beat2: A Bitcoin candlestick chart drawn in WebGL, one particle at a time. Same kind of data that becomes game terrain in Candle Cross — because pretty data is worth nothing until it becomes a product.

manifesto.statement: I don't ship pretty screens. I ship products that survive their second month in production.
manifesto.paragraph1: I've been a software engineer for over nine years, specialized in React and React Native. I work inside teams — modernizing production apps used daily in retail — and alone, from scratch, on my own products.
manifesto.paragraph2: In practice: I pick the payment integration thinking about Pix and Brazilian invoicing, I hunt 1,472ms of INP down to the guilty listener, I upgrade dependencies in waves that revert with a single command. And I write the decision down, because a year from now someone will ask why.
manifesto.pullquote: Good software is the software that still makes sense the day you have to change it.

aboutPage.seoTitle: About André Bordignon — freelance developer in Brazil
aboutPage.seoDescription: Nine years building web and mobile: who I am, where I work, how I work and with what stack. A fact sheet and the disciplines, no fluff.
aboutPage.title: Who's on the other side of the code.
aboutPage.story1: I started programming professionally in 2017 and never drifted far from the product. I've worked in agency teams, on internal products and directly with clients, and the conclusion was always the same: what separates good software from expensive software is how many wrong decisions you avoid before the first line.
aboutPage.story2: Today I split my time between team work — modernizing production React Native apps in retail — and my own products, where I'm the product, the design, the code and the support. That second half is what taught me to think about operating cost, billing and churn, not just components.
aboutPage.story3: I'm based in Brasília and work remotely across Brazil. I work with a written scope before starting, a preview on every delivery, and technical decisions written down — because a year from now someone will ask why, and I want to have the answer.
aboutPage.pullquote: I don't subcontract. You talk to the person writing the code.

cta.title: Tell me what you want to build.
cta.body: A 30-minute conversation about the problem usually settles more than three email threads about technology. If it isn't for me, I'll say so right away.
